questions.q: Under cash accounting, when is revenue recorded?
options: When cash is actually received
When the work is substantially completed
At the start of the fiscal year, regardless of activity
Cash accounting never records revenue
questions.explain: Cash accounting records revenue only when cash is received, regardless of when the underlying work was performed.

questions.q: Ridgeview Advisory Partners completes a $10,000 project on December 28 but is paid on January 10. Under accrual accounting, when is the $10,000 of revenue recorded?
options: January, when the cash arrives
Split evenly between December and January
December, when the work was earned/completed
It is never recorded under accrual accounting
questions.explain: Accrual accounting records revenue when it is earned, which was December in this example, regardless of when cash was collected.

questions.q: Why can cash accounting give a misleading picture of a period's performance?
options: Because cash accounting always overstates revenue
Because cash accounting is illegal in every country
Because cash accounting requires more journal entries than accrual accounting
Because it ties revenue and expenses to the sometimes-random timing of cash movement rather than to when the real economic activity occurred
questions.explain: Cash accounting can make a highly productive period look empty (or vice versa) simply because of when cash happened to move.

questions.q: Which accounting basis do GAAP and most accounting standards require for businesses beyond the smallest scale?
options: Cash basis
Accrual basis
Neither basis is required by any standard
A fifty-fifty blend of both bases
questions.explain: GAAP and most standards require accrual-basis financial statements for any business beyond the smallest scale.

questions.q: How is Oracle Fusion Financials architected with respect to accrual and cash accounting?
options: It is built entirely around accrual accounting; cash-basis reporting, when needed, is typically derived from the accrual-basis books
It is built entirely around cash accounting, with accrual as an optional add-on
It supports neither accrual nor cash accounting
It alternates between the two bases automatically each month
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion Financials is architected around the accrual model; any cash-basis view is generally derived from the underlying accrual-basis records.
